x-derived-from: The shipped code of both builds (Rust consolidation b1b7ec2 incl. the scene guard; Python living tree 6f830e5), extracted field-by-field in extract-rust.md / extract-python.md beside this file, and verified against the live tools/list of both servers by harness/contract_check.py.
x-descriptions: Tool description/docstring prose is NOT part of this contract. The builds word their descriptions independently (Rust: terse wire copy; Python: long docstrings). The contract pins names, argument types, fields, grades, and codes — not prose.

notes: cost_counted_usd / call_made are NOT universal error extras: they appear only on the codes whose call flow counted spend (documented per code in the extracts). NOT_CONFIGURED, BAD_ARGUMENT, NO_CONCEPT, NOT_A_SOURCE_PHOTO carry neither.
FIDELITY_VIOLATION puts output_asset / fidelity_receipt / cost_usd INSIDE the error object in both builds (Rust: cost_usd, not cost_counted_usd).

Spend-cap refusal is a result code in Rust (SPEND_CAP_REFUSED, message starts "Spend cap") and an exception in Python (ledger.SpendCapExceeded / SpendCapExceededAtSettle, message prefix "SPEND CAP EXCEEDED at settle: ..."). Recorded as a mechanism difference, not a wording contract.
envelope.shape: {status: "error", tool, <echo/null fields>, error: {code, message, ...extras inside error}}

exception_carried.rust: Propagated Err(String) becomes JSON-RPC {code: -32603, message}; contained panics surface as "<tool> failed (internal fault contained; the server is still running)".

cut.classification: intentional, documented asymmetry: grading lives in the Python reference build; the Rust build carries the measured counts and lets the caller decide. A client must not expect a grade from the Rust build.
cut.python: Present: mask_review.cut_quality on every cut_out result; receipt cut_quality.before/after on every v4 draw receipt (after.grade is always PASS).
cut.rust: ABSENT from tool results and from the fidelity receipt. The only Rust grade is the room-run ownership record cut_quality.grade in {PASS, RESHOOT} (no REPAIRABLE), which is not part of the MCP tool surface.

plate.classification: intentional, documented asymmetry, as for cut grades.
plate.python: Present inside receipt plate_quality.assessment and attempts[].quality (v4 receipts).
plate.rust: ABSENT (no plate grade block; plate outcomes surface as result fields and error codes).

x-purpose: One written contract for the agenthand MCP interface: tool names and argument types, result and receipt fields per receipt schema version, the grade vocabularies, and the error-code vocabularies. Two independent implementations (Rust product, Python reference) are tested against this file. Where the builds intentionally differ, the difference is recorded here as data (x-differences); a difference that is not recorded here fails the contract tests.

cut_out.notes: mask_review differs inside: Rust has exactly {mask_pixels, coverage, bbox, bbox_fill, touches_frame_edges, warnings}; Python carries those (coverage/bbox_fill rounded to 6dp) PLUS cut_quality (the cut grade block) and dropped_component_pixels. attempts items share {phrase, records, outcome} with outcome in {accepted, no_match, poor_mask, unparseable}; Python items also carry tile/sam_width/sam_height/scale_method.

placeholder.both: plate_asset: null; no usage and no call_id on the result in EITHER build; fidelity_receipt plate_kind/plate_source are "local_placeholder".
placeholder.divergence: Rust placeholder results carry no verify_url/label/qr_asset unless the QR sidecar succeeded (conditional); Python placeholder results always carry verify_url/label. The persisted placeholder receipts still validate against receipt_v2_rust / receipt_v4_python respectively (Python's carries usage as the stub's 4-key zero object and call_id; Rust's placeholder ledger row has status "stub").

identify.notes: usage is the 4-key object in both builds. Error results: same echo/null skeleton in both; Python adds concept_rewritten_from: null.

x-transport.python: Tools return the result dict directly (the MCP SDK wraps it); draw success returns [result_dict, Image], draw errors return the bare dict. Exception-carried failures (PLATE_REJECTED, RESHOOT_REQUIRED, SpendCapExceeded, FidelityLockError, KeyError) propagate as MCP tool errors, never as result dicts.
x-transport.rust: tools/call returns {content: [text JSON, ...], structuredContent: <result object>, isError: false}; isError is false even for status:"error" results; draw success appends an image content block. Propagated internal errors become a JSON-RPC error {code: -32603, message}.
